role.altitude: The environmental technician keeps inspecting sites, judging which measures are needed, validating methods and designing waste programs; looking up limit values, compiling data, rerunning statistics and copying contractor figures shrink.
skills_to_grow: Maintaining analysis scripts and checking their output
role.ambitious_version: A technician whose statistics update the day new results arrive, leaving time for site visits.

tasks.short: Inspect the site and measure conditions, look up the limit values and control measures that apply, judge which measures are needed, write recommendations to control or eliminate unsafe conditions, have them approved and send them.

steps.what: Environmental technician inspects the site and measures unsafe conditions
Environmental technician looks up the limit values and control measures that apply
Environmental technician judges which measures are needed to control or eliminate unsafe conditions
Environmental technician writes the recommendations report
Environmental scientist approves the final recommendations report
Environmental technician sends the approved report to the site manager

approvals.approved_version: the recommendations report as approved by the environmental scientist in s5; any change goes back for approval

tasks.design: Limit values and standard control measures sit in a table per substance and hazard kept by the team, so the technician looks them up by name instead of searching documents. Inspecting, measuring and judging the measures stay with the technician. The report template fills site details, measurements and limits from the measurement record, and the technician writes the recommendations. The scientist approves before sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Limits were searched in several documents and copied into each report.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintained limit-value tables and report templates.
tasks.still_hard: Conditions with no clear limit value.
tasks.human_edge: Proposing a measure the site will actually carry out.
tasks.altitude: Less looking up and copying; judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether clearer reports lead to faster action.

evidence.claim: Calculations and comparisons against fixed limits are plain code.

assumptions: Boundary: from inspection to recommendations sent; carrying out measures is the site's.
Input contract for s2: a limit-value table kept current by the environmental scientist.
Inspection, judgement and sending keep their full time; the scientist's time is outside the technician's savings.

incremental.description: Environmental technician reports outdated entries in the limit table.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual hazards with no standard measures; high: routine inspections with standard substances.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review standard methods and requirements, develop testing procedures, validate them in the lab or field, have them approved and release them with instruction for colleagues.

steps.what: Environmental technician reviews standard methods and requirements
Environmental technician develops the testing procedure in writing
Environmental technician validates the procedure in the lab or field
Environmental scientist approves the final procedure
Environmental technician releases the procedure and instructs colleagues

tasks.design: Procedures are written in the lab's standard template in the document system, which keeps versions, approval and read receipts, so earlier procedures can be reused and release is a status change rather than a mail-out. Reviewing methods, writing the steps and validating stay with the technician; the scientist approves.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures were written from scratch in loose documents and circulated by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Document systems with templates, versions and read receipts.
tasks.still_hard: New contaminants with no standard method.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which step will go wrong in the field.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; admin around procedures shrinks.

reach.learn: Whether current procedures are easier to find.

evidence.claim: Official control labs must be accredited; the standard requires validated methods and software.
A lab system generates certificates with e-signatures and audit trails.

assumptions: Boundary: developing and releasing a testing procedure; routine testing is outside.
Validation keeps its full time; the scientist's time is outside the technician's savings.
unknowns: How many procedures are developed per year.
research_questions: Do audit findings on procedures fall?

incremental.description: Environmental technician keeps the procedure template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new methods built from scratch; high: updates of existing procedures.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile lab and field data, perform statistical analysis of environmental data, judge significance and outliers, and prepare tables and charts for the scientist.

steps.what: Environmental technician compiles lab results and field readings into a dataset
Environmental technician runs descriptive statistics and trend tests
Environmental technician judges significance, outliers and data quality
Environmental technician prepares tables and charts for the scientist

tasks.design: Lab results export from the lab system and logger readings from the field loggers into one analysis dataset by script instead of copy-paste. A saved analysis script runs the agreed descriptive statistics and trend tests per delivery, and table and chart scripts write the outputs. Judging significance, outliers and data quality stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were pasted together and analysed afresh in spreadsheets each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Lab system exports and scripted analyses.
tasks.still_hard: Values below detection limits and changing methods.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that an odd value is a sampling error, not pollution.

ambition.what: Update trend analyses with every delivery instead of once a year.

evidence.claim: A lab system barcodes samples, assigns tests and logs each change.
Calculations over fixed formulas are plain code.

assumptions: Boundary: analysing a monitoring dataset; interpretation for decisions is the scientist's.
Input contract for s1: results exported from the lab system and readings from field loggers, about 80% of data; manual field notes are typed; s1 is priced at that share.
unknowns: Share of data from manual field notes.

already_counted.description: Environmental technician checks script output against a known dataset after changes.

incremental.description: Environmental technician maintains the analysis scripts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off studies with mixed data; high: recurring monitoring with the same data layout.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Survey waste streams on site, gather waste volumes and costs, design and implement site recycling or hazardous waste stream programs, and check and sign waste transport documents.

steps.what: Environmental technician surveys the site's waste streams in person
Environmental technician gathers waste volumes and costs from the contractor's reports
Environmental technician designs the recycling or hazardous waste stream program
Environmental technician implements the program: instructs staff, labels containers and arranges collection
Environmental technician checks and signs hazardous waste transport documents

tasks.design: The waste contractor's portal exports weights and costs per stream and container, which load into the site's waste overview instead of being copied from invoices and weighing slips. Transport documents arrive prefilled from the contractor's data for the technician to check and sign. Surveying, designing and implementing the program stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Volumes were copied from invoices and weighing slips.
tasks.enabler_now: Contractor portals with exports per stream.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed waste that staff do not separate.
tasks.human_edge: Getting staff to change how they throw things away.

evidence.claim: Spreadsheets between systems are the glue today; integrations replace re-keying.

assumptions: Boundary: designing and running a site waste program; processing waste is the contractor's.
Input contract for s2: weights and costs per stream from the contractor's weighbridge and billing, exported monthly; about 80% of streams go through the main contractor; s2 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s5: transport documents prefilled by the contractor.
Survey, design and implementation keep their full time.

incremental.description: Environmental technician maps new contractor stream codes to the site overview.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: sites with several small contractors; high: one main contractor with good exports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
